sections.title: PHP and the end of passwords

items.q: What did they read from the FBI about PHP?
items.a: Joe pulls up an **FBI Cyber Division** note: **two critical PHP vulnerabilities** could let attackers **remotely execute code** in PHP's core and compromise data and networks. He puts the hole at about **14 years**.

items.q: What does Joe say that means for passwords?
items.a: AI will **figure out the code of everything that exists**. Then **encryption is gone** and **passwords are useless**, because the money is already online.

items.q: What does Kurt separate in the Vince Foster story?
items.a: He recommends **The Strange Death of Vince Foster** and describes **missing blood**, a **body that had been moved**, and a **gun still in the hand**. **Gary Webb**, not Foster, is the one he says was shot **twice**.

items.q: Who does Kurt say wrote that account?
items.a: He names **Chris Ruddy**, now of **Newsmax**, and relays an interview claiming Ruddy **helped cover the case up**. Joe's reaction is that the book he trusted now has to be **rethought**.

items.q: Why does Midnight Gospel look psychedelic on purpose?
items.a: **Pendleton Ward** told the animators **not to sweat the model grid**. Off-model frames read as **more psychedelic**, and he let anyone in the room **pitch an idea**.

items.q: Where does Duncan say AI fits in that kind of show?
items.a: It can speed **in-betweens**. It does not replace a room of artists whose **disagreement and struggle produce the sparks**. One or two people with a model will not match that group.

items.q: What do they say Cambridge Analytica actually harvested?
items.a: A quiz app took the quiz-taker **and their friends**. They read a figure of up to **87 million** Facebook profiles, used for **Trump and Cruz in 2016** and for **Brexit**. Kurt calls that **regular stuff now** — the same trick that sells you a TV.

items.q: How do they say search does the same job today?
items.a: Results are **curated**: one candidate's query leads with the **negative stories**, another's with the **flattering ones**. They cite a **$5 billion** Facebook penalty and a New Mexico order they say just hit **Meta** for **$25 billion**.
